title: Illustration / Characters / Noses / Angles
slide_intent: Adapt a feature to viewing angle so the face reads as one form turning in space.
strategic_value: A consistent transition from frontal to profile construction can help Duolingo keep characters recognizable across poses.
demonstration: Two rows show a head in front, three-quarter and profile views; side text states how the nose edge and color change.
practical_value: Check nose edge direction in three-quarter view and remove its contrasting color in profile.

content_islands.name: Angle sequences
content_islands.spec: Arrange two three-view head sequences at left, moving from front through three-quarter to profile.

content_islands.name: View-specific rules
content_islands.spec: Place the Angles heading and two instructions at right, distinguishing three-quarter geometry from profile color.

reference_purposes.Application: The two sequences demonstrate the same nose behavior across different head shapes.
reference_purposes.Constraint: In three-quarter view the right nose edge angles outward while the left becomes vertical; in profile the nose takes the base skin color.

ingredient.name: Nose behavior across views
ingredient.role: Keep facial construction coherent as the head turns.
ingredient.application: In the displayed three-quarter view, angle the right nose edge outward and keep the left edge vertical; in profile match the nose to the skin.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. Directional wording follows the source’s illustrated orientation; it is not a universal screen-space rule for every mirrored pose.
